paragraphs.source_en: Leon V strengthened the walls, especially around Blachernai (close to the Golden 484 Resilience and Recovery Horn), and he sent envoys to Aachen to seek an anti-​Bulgar alliance. They found that Charlemagne had died in February. When they returned, they found that Krum had died too, in April, of a cerebral hemorrhage (“streams of blood had poured out of his mouth, nose, and ears”). Leon circulated a notice throughout the realm claiming that the khan had died of the wound he received during the ambush of the previous year.77 Harun al-​Rashid had died in 809 and his heirs had already begun to fight among themselves. The three great rivals to the Roman emperor had all died within a few years. Despite recent defeats on the battlefield, Romanía was well positioned to come out ahead.
